result.topic_en: An estimate in the theory of integral equations with kernel K: from a bound on an integral involving g, v, K and h, Hilbert derives that the integral of (f - f*)^2 is small, with a large crossed-out failed attempt in the middle of the page.
result.transcription:
$\left|\int_a^b K(s,t)\left(g(t) - v(t)\int_a^b K(t,r) [-\ldots-] h(r)\,dr\right)^{*} dt\right| < \sqrt{\varepsilon''}\int_a^b K^2(s,t)\,dt$
und folglich
[-$= f^{*}(s)$-]
$\int_a^b K(s,t) g(t)\,dt = \int_a^b\int_a^b [-\ldots-] K(s,t)\, v(t)\, K(t,r)\, h(r)\,dr + \vartheta\sqrt{\varepsilon''}\int_a^b K^2(s,t)\,dt$
$^{*}(-1 \leq \vartheta \leq 1)$
[-und daher wegen (1)
$\int_a^b \left\{ f(s) - v(s)\int_a^b\int_a^b K(s,t) v(t) K(t,r) h(r)\,dr - \vartheta\sqrt{\ldots}\right\}^2 ds < \varepsilon$
oder
$\int_a^b (f(s) - f^{*}(s))^2 ds < \varepsilon' + 2\sqrt{\varepsilon''}\int_a^b (f(s) - f^{*}(s))\vartheta\sqrt{\int_a^b K^2 dt}\, ds - \varepsilon''\int_a^b \vartheta^2 (\int K^2 dt)\, ds$
und da

wir

setzen, so wird wegen (1)
(2) $\int_a^b \left(f(s) - f^{*}(s) - \vartheta\sqrt{\varepsilon''}\, M_b\right)^2 ds < \varepsilon'$
